title: Pirates & the Human Body 🏴‍☠️
description: Learn body parts vocabulary, practice singular and irregular plurals, and master 'have got' vs 'has got' descriptions.
subject: Englisch

blocks.content:
# Pirates & Body Parts

Ahoy, mateys! Let's meet Captain Hook. He is a famous pirate.

### 'Have got' vs. 'Has got' Grammar:
- **I / We / You / They** -> have got (haven't got)
- **He / She / It** -> has got (hasn't got)

*Examples*:
- I **have got** two arms.
- The pirate **has got** an eye patch.

3. A skeleton pirate ((hasn't got)) any skin or hair.
4. I ((have got)) two eyes, but the cyclops pirate ((has got)) only one.
5. We ((have got)) a treasure map! Let's find the gold.

title: At the Zoo: Animals & Prepositions 🦁
description: Learn zoo animals spelling, practice conjugating 'to be' (am/is/are), and master spatial prepositions (in, on, under, next to).
subject: Englisch

blocks.content:
# Zoo Animals & Prepositions

### The Verb 'to be':
- **I** -> am
- **He / She / It** -> is
- **We / You / They** -> are

### Prepositions of Place:
- **in**: inside something (e.g. *in the water*)
- **on**: on top of something (e.g. *on the tree*)
- **under**: beneath something (e.g. *under the rock*)
- **next to**: beside something (e.g. *next to the elephant*)

3. The giraffe ((is)) very tall and has a long neck.
4. Elephants ((aren't)) small, they are huge!
5. Lions ((are)) dangerous cats. A lion ((isn't)) a pet.

title: School Grammar: Plurals & Numbers 📐

blocks.content:
# Plurals & Numbers

### Plural Rules:
- **Most nouns**: Add `-s` (e.g. *pen -> pens*)
- **Nouns ending in -s, -sh, -ch, -x**: Add `-es` (e.g. *box -> boxes*)
- **Irregulars**: Learn them! (*child -> children*, *man -> men*, *foot -> feet*)

### Numbers 1 - 25:
1 one, 2 two, 3 three, 4 four, 5 five, 6 six, 7 seven, 8 eight, 9 nine, 10 ten, 11 eleven, 12 twelve, 13 thirteen, 14 fourteen, 15 fifteen, 16 sixteen, 17 seventeen, 18 eighteen, 19 nineteen, 20 twenty... 25 twenty-five.

2. We need three ((boxes)) for the books. (box)
3. There are four ((children)) in the playground. (child)
4. Touch your two ((feet))! (foot)
5. The teacher has five red ((pens)). (pen)

title: Present Perfect vs. Past Simple
description: Interactive grammar quiz testing the difference between actions completed in the past and actions related to the present.
subject: Englisch

blocks.content:
# Present Perfect vs. Past Simple

Remember:
- **Past Simple**: Used for completed actions in the past with a specific time word (e.g., *yesterday, in 2020, 5 minutes ago*).
- **Present Perfect**: Used for life experiences, actions with a connection to the present, or when the exact time is not important (e.g., *already, yet, never, ever*).

blocks.template:
1. I ((saw)) a great movie yesterday. (see)
2. She ((has already finished)) her homework, so she can play now. (already / finish)
3. We ((went)) to London last summer. (go)
4. They ((have lived)) in Telfs for five years. (live)

# Prepositions of Time & Place

Use:
- **IN**: months, years, seasons, parts of the day, enclosed spaces.
- **ON**: days of the week, dates, surfaces.
- **AT**: specific times, specific locations.

title: Active vs. Passive Voice Challenge
description: Advanced grammar worksheets testing active and passive sentence transformations.
subject: Englisch

blocks.content:
# Active vs. Passive Voice

How to form the passive voice:
- **Object + Form of 'to be' + Past Participle (3rd form)**.
- *Active*: "The cat chased the mouse."
- *Passive*: "The mouse was chased by the cat."

blocks.instruction: Select all sentences that are in the PASSIVE voice:
options: Grandma baked a delicious chocolate cake.
A new school is being constructed in Telfs.
We have played football all afternoon.

blocks.instruction: Transform the active sentences into passive voice:
blocks.template:
1. Active: 'They clean the classrooms every day.'
   Passive: 'The classrooms ((are cleaned)) every day.'

2. Active: 'Leo wrote the essay.'
   Passive: 'The essay ((was written)) by Leo.'

3. Active: 'She will buy the tickets.'
   Passive: 'The tickets ((will be bought)) by her.'

title: Bruchrechnen Grundlagen
description: Übungen zum Erweitern, Kürzen und Addieren von einfachen Brüchen.
subject: Mathematik

blocks.content:
# Einführung in Brüche
Ein Bruch besteht aus einem Zähler (oben) und einem Nenner (unten). Zum Beispiel: $$\frac{1}{2}$$.

- **Kürzen**: Zähler und Nenner durch dieselbe Zahl teilen.
- **Erweitern**: Zähler und Nenner mit derselben Zahl multiplizieren.

blocks.instruction: Kürze oder erweitere die Brüche richtig:
blocks.template:
1. Erweitere $$\frac{1}{2}$$ mit 3: $$\frac{((3))}{((6))}$$
2. Kürze $$\frac{4}{8}$$ so weit wie möglich: $$\frac{((1))}{((2))}$$

title: Die Pflanzenzelle
description: Struktur und Funktion der wichtigsten Organellen einer pflanzlichen Zelle.
subject: Biologie

blocks.content:
# Die pflanzliche Zelle
Pflanzenzellen unterscheiden sich von Tierzellen vor allem durch drei Dinge:
1. **Zellwand**: Gibt der Zelle Stabilität.
2. **Vakuole**: Speichert Wasser und Nährstoffe.
3. **Chloroplasten**: Verantwortlich für die Fotosynthese (enthalten Blattgrün).

description: Lerne die chemischen Elemente, Symbole und Ordnungszahlen kennen.
subject: Chemie

blocks.content:
# Das Periodensystem der Elemente (PSE)
Die Elemente sind nach ihrer Ordnungszahl sortiert. Jedes Element hat ein Symbol:
- **H**: Wasserstoff (Ordnungszahl 1)
- **He**: Helium (Ordnungszahl 2)
- **O**: Sauerstoff (Ordnungszahl 8)
- **C**: Kohlenstoff (Ordnungszahl 6)

title: Der elektrische Stromkreis
description: Grundlagen zu Stromstärke, Spannung, Widerstand und Reihen-/Parallelschaltungen.
subject: Physik

blocks.content:
# Der Stromkreis
Ein einfacher Stromkreis besteht aus einer Spannungsquelle (z.B. Batterie), Leitern (Kabeln) und einem Verbraucher (z.B. Glühbirne).
- **Spannung (U)** wird in Volt (V) gemessen.
- **Stromstärke (I)** wird in Ampere (A) gemessen.
- **Widerstand (R)** wird in Ohm (\Omega) gemessen.
Es gilt das Ohmsche Gesetz: $$U = R \cdot I$$.
